To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antioxidant activity and the total phenolic content of Northern Italian mono- (Casaliva) and multi-variet (organic and non-organic) extra virgin olive oils, after early and late harvest, were analyzed.
the organic mono-culture Casaliva E.V.O.O. from early harvest showed the best antioxidant properties, mainly due to the higher content of secoridoids and tocopherols.
the organic Casaliva mono-cultivar EVOO harvested in early season, is the best candidate for the exploitation of the antioxidant properties of the EVOOs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the antioxidant properties of some secondary metabolites in Northern Italian mono- or multi-varietal EVOOs, after early and late harvest.
the identification of the most interesting EVOOs in terms of phenolic content, antioxidant activity, α-tocopherols, and the most interesting EPOs for the production of high-quality EVOO.
a better understanding of the antioxidant properties of EVOOs, which may be useful to improve their quality and their potential use in functional food.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the early harvest EVOO, in particular the mono-cultivar organic Casaliva, represents the best choice for a high phenolic and α-Tocopherol content, and for the most important antioxidant properties, as well.
, among the tested EVOO varieties, Casaliva ECOO (early harvested) is the best choice in terms of antioxidant properties.
the early harvest organic Casaliva E.V.O. is a good candidate to be considered a functional food.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the early harvest, organic Casaliva mono-varietal EVOO is the best choice among the studied samples in order to maximize the antioxidant properties, mainly due to the higher SIDs fraction, and the α-tocopherols content.
the organic Casaliva E.V. olive oil from Northern Italy has the highest total phenol content (326.19 mg/Kg) and antioxidant capacity (1285.97 ORAC units).
early harvest, mono-cultivar EVOOs, particularly Casaliva, are the best choice to maximize the health benefits related to their antioxidant properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antioxidant properties of EVOO can vary depending on the variety, the olive ripeness at harvest, and whether the oil is mono- or multi-varietal, and whether it is organic or not.
early harvest EVOO is more effective in terms of antioxidant capacity and phenolic content than late harvest.

the organic mono-culivar EVOO from the early harvest of Casaliva olives is a promising source of phenolic compounds, which may contribute to a reduced risk of chronic diseases associated with oxidative stress.
